files.regeneration_mechanism: cmake/QtGnCredits.cmake runs tools/licenses/licenses.py in 'credits' mode with --gn-target=:QtWebEngineCore and --gn-out-dir=<BUILDDIR>, no --gn-generate flag (so licenses.py requires BUILDDIR to already contain a real `gn gen`-produced build.ninja for that target -- see tools/licenses/licenses.py FindThirdPartyDeps()). This is wired into Qt's own build as add_dependencies(generate_chromium_attributions run_core_GnDone) in src/core/api/CMakeLists.txt. It is standalone third-party source processing in the sense that no OrbitRx/PySide application source is involved -- only Qt's own qtwebengine-everywhere tree plus a Qt host toolchain -- but it is not a bare licenses.py-over-the-tree operation; it requires a genuinely GN-generated out directory for the exact target.
files.fidelity_requirement: To match Qt's own target-filtered attributions for the actual shipped (Windows/MSVC) binary, the GN args used to generate that out dir must match the production args.gn. A captured production log reference (third_party/qt/qtwebengine-core-gn-log.txt, from GitHub Actions run 42476475449, showing is_msvc=true) is mentioned in old-offer-draft.md; docs/REGENERATE_CREDITS.sh and .ps1 both support diffing against such a log via the PRODUCTION_GN_ARGS_FILE environment variable and will print FIDELITY: PASS/WARN/NOT CHECKED accordingly.
